## Introduction

If BGE's existing heat pump homes moved from Schedule R to Schedule R-HP, BGE would collect
less distribution, transmission and EmPOWER revenue from them. This notebook estimates that
shortfall and what it would add to the rates and bills of everyone still on Schedule R.

This is a simplified, static, one-year estimate on the test-year rates. It follows the
Connecticut method (Lee's CIEC-3 and CIEC-6 responses), with three differences for Maryland:

- **Only existing heat pump homes create a shortfall.** Today's Schedule R rates recover the
  residential class's embedded costs from today's customers, fossil-heated homes included. A
  home that adds a heat pump and moves to R-HP keeps paying at least its old bill, plus the
  marginal cost of its new load, which R-HP's rates are calibrated to cover on average. It
  still pays the share of embedded costs it was assigned, so it shifts nothing onto others.
  An existing heat pump home is different: it already pays Schedule R's full rate, so moving
  it to R-HP cuts revenue BGE collects today. New adopters are set to zero.
- **R-HP is flat and year-round.** It replaces three volumetric charges in every month:
  distribution, Rider 1 transmission and Rider 8 EmPOWER. Connecticut's Rate HP changes only
  winter distribution and transmission.
- **Electric resistance homes stay on Schedule R** and are in the group that pays.

The range of results comes from **how many homes enroll**. The counts come from
[`bge_hp_customer_estimate.qmd`](bge_hp_customer_estimate.qmd), so that notebook is rendered
first. The **load profile** of an enrolled home is a second, parallel choice, so we show one
table for each of two profiles.

```{python}
#| label: setup

from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import yaml
from great_tables import GT, html, md, style
from great_tables import loc as gt_loc
from IPython.display import Markdown

from lib.great_tables import get_switchbox_gt_tab_options
from lib.quarto import display_gt
from lib.rates_analysis.rate_case_funcs import (
    load_billing_kwh_annual,
    load_master_bills,
    segment_name,
    segment_upgrade,
)
from lib.rdp import fetch_rdp_file

PATH_CACHE = Path("../cache")
PATH_CCAN_1_4 = Path("../../../context/sources/md_hp_rates/mdpuc_9888_bge_ccandr01_04_attachment_1.xlsx")
_batch_config = yaml.safe_load(Path("../batch_config.yaml").read_text())
STATE = _batch_config["STATE"]
BATCH = _batch_config["BATCH"]
RDP_REF = _batch_config["RDP_REF"]
RESSTOCK_RELEASE = _batch_config["RESSTOCK_RELEASE"]
UTILITY = "bge"

SEG_R_PRECALC = segment_name(_batch_config["BASELINE_BILL_SCENARIO"], "precalc")
SEG_R_CALIBRATED = segment_name(_batch_config["BASELINE_BILL_SCENARIO"], "calibrated")
SEG_RHP_PRECALC = segment_name(_batch_config["RHP_BILL_SCENARIO"], "precalc")

PATH_RATES_R = "rate_design/hp_rates/md/config/rev_requirement/top-ups/monthly_rates/bge_monthly_rates_2025.yaml"
PATH_RATES_RHP = "rate_design/hp_rates/md/config/tariffs/electric/custom_rates/bge_rhp_flat.yaml"
PATH_RR = "rate_design/hp_rates/md/config/rev_requirement/bge_large_number_rate_case_test_year.yaml"
PATH_RR_TEST_YEAR = "rate_design/hp_rates/md/config/rev_requirement/bge_rate_case_test_year.yaml"
RDP_BLOB = f"https://github.com/switchbox-data/rate-design-platform/blob/{RDP_REF}"
LINK_RATES_R = Markdown(f"[Schedule R rates]({RDP_BLOB}/{PATH_RATES_R})")
LINK_RATES_RHP = Markdown(f"[proposed R-HP rates]({RDP_BLOB}/{PATH_RATES_RHP})")

COMPONENTS = ["Distribution", "Transmission", "EmPOWER"]

report_vars: dict = {}


def dollar(x: float, accuracy: int = 0) -> str:
    """Dollar text for inline values, which Quarto inserts as plain text."""
    return f"${x:,.{accuracy}f}"


def cents(x: float, accuracy: int = 3) -> str:
    """``x`` is in $/kWh."""
    return f"{x * 100:,.{accuracy}f}¢"


def pct(x: float, accuracy: int = 1) -> str:
    return f"{x * 100:,.{accuracy}f}%"


def num(x: float) -> str:
    return f"{round(x):,}"
```

## Customers and total kWh from CAIRO

We take customer weights and billed kWh from CAIRO batch `{python} BATCH`, the run behind
the direct testimony. CAIRO rescales ResStock's sample weights so they sum to BGE's test-year
residential customer count from Karas Exhibit E-3. Raw ResStock metadata weights don't
have that scaling, so we read the weights from the master bills.

```{python}
#| label: weights

weights = (
    load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, SEG_R_PRECALC)
    .filter(pl.col("month") == "Annual", pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY)
    .select(
        "bldg_id",
        "weight",
        pl.col("postprocess_group.has_hp").alias("has_hp"),
        pl.col("postprocess_group.heating_type_v2").alias("heating_type"),
    )
    .collect()
)
customers = float(weights["weight"].sum())
_rr = yaml.safe_load(fetch_rdp_file(PATH_RR, ref=RDP_REF))
if abs(customers - _rr["test_year_customer_count"]) > 1:
    raise RuntimeError(f"CAIRO weights sum to {customers:,.0f}, not {_rr['test_year_customer_count']:,.0f}")
if weights["bldg_id"].n_unique() != weights.height:
    raise RuntimeError("Duplicate buildings in master bills")
report_vars["customers"] = customers
weights.group_by("heating_type", "has_hp").agg(pl.len().alias("buildings"), pl.col("weight").sum().alias("customers"))
```

The kWh that still pays is the weighted sum of each building's annual billed grid kWh.

```{python}
#| label: total-kwh

annual_kwh_r = load_billing_kwh_annual(STATE, UTILITY, BATCH, SEG_R_PRECALC).collect()
_joined = annual_kwh_r.join(weights, on="bldg_id", how="inner")
if _joined.height != weights.height:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Annual kWh joined {_joined.height} of {weights.height} buildings")
kwh_total = float((_joined["annual_kwh_grid"] * _joined["weight"]).sum())

# Karas Exhibit E-3: Schedule R + RL test-year kWh, from the rate-case budget config.
kwh_test_year = float(yaml.safe_load(fetch_rdp_file(PATH_RR_TEST_YEAR, ref=RDP_REF))["test_year_residential_kwh"])
if _rr["resstock_kwh_scale_factor"] != 1:
    raise RuntimeError("This batch scales ResStock kWh; revisit the kWh caveat below")
kwh_ratio = kwh_test_year / kwh_total
report_vars.update(kwh_total=kwh_total, kwh_test_year=kwh_test_year, kwh_ratio=kwh_ratio)
print(f"CAIRO billed residential kWh: {kwh_total / 1e9:,.2f} TWh")
print(f"BGE test-year residential kWh (Karas E-3): {kwh_test_year / 1e9:,.2f} TWh")
print(f"Ratio (BGE / CAIRO): {kwh_ratio:.3f}")
```

The batch's revenue-requirement config sets `resstock_kwh_scale_factor` to 1, so CAIRO
bills ResStock's unscaled kWh: `{python} f"{kwh_total / 1e9:,.2f}"` TWh, against BGE's
test-year `{python} f"{kwh_test_year / 1e9:,.2f}"` TWh. The per-kWh charge below is not
affected by a uniform gap, because the shortfall and the kWh that pays come from the same
run. The dollar shortfall and the mean bill are at ResStock's usage, so they are high by that
gap; multiply them by `{python} f"{kwh_ratio:.3f}"` to put them on BGE's sales.

## Rates

Schedule R's volumetric rates change during BGE's April 2025 to March 2026 rate year, so we
flatten each one to an annual flat rate: the simple average of its 12 monthly rates.
Distribution is the core delivery rate plus the environmental surcharge, which is how the R-HP
distribution rate is defined. R-HP replaces these three charges with flat rates. The customer
charge, universal service charge and generation stay on Schedule R, so they drop out of the
difference.

```{python}
#| label: rates

_rates_r = yaml.safe_load(fetch_rdp_file(PATH_RATES_R, ref=RDP_REF))
_charges_r = {**_rates_r["add_to_drr"]["charges"], **_rates_r["already_in_drr"]["charges"]}


def _annual_flat(*names: str) -> float:
    """Simple average over the rate year of the sum of the named monthly charges."""
    total = 0.0
    for name in names:
        monthly = _charges_r[name]["monthly_rates"]
        if len(monthly) != 12:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: expected 12 monthly rates, got {len(monthly)}")
        total += sum(float(rate) for rate in monthly.values()) / 12
    return total


schedule_r_flat = {
    "Distribution": _annual_flat("core_delivery_rate", "environmental_surcharge"),
    "Transmission": _annual_flat("transmission_rate_adjustment"),
    "EmPOWER": _annual_flat("empower_maryland_charge"),
}

_rhp = yaml.safe_load(fetch_rdp_file(PATH_RATES_RHP, ref=RDP_REF))["delivery"]
rhp_flat = {
    "Distribution": float(_rhp["delivery_service"]),
    "Transmission": float(_rhp["transmission"]),
    "EmPOWER": float(_rhp["energy_efficiency"]),
}
_flat_charge_names = ["core_delivery_rate", "environmental_surcharge", "transmission_rate_adjustment", "empower_maryland_charge"]
monthly_r_total = {
    month: sum(float(_charges_r[name]["monthly_rates"][month]) for name in _flat_charge_names)
    for month in _charges_r["core_delivery_rate"]["monthly_rates"]
}

discount = {name: schedule_r_flat[name] - rhp_flat[name] for name in COMPONENTS}
discount["Total"] = sum(discount.values())
report_vars.update(schedule_r_flat=schedule_r_flat, rhp_flat=rhp_flat, discount=discount)

pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "component": [*COMPONENTS, "Total"],
        "schedule_r_flat": [*schedule_r_flat.values(), sum(schedule_r_flat.values())],
        "rhp_flat": [*rhp_flat.values(), sum(rhp_flat.values())],
        "discount": list(discount.values()),
    }
)
```

On an annual flat basis, Schedule R charges `{python} cents(sum(schedule_r_flat.values()), 2)`
per kWh for the three charges combined and R-HP charges
`{python} cents(sum(rhp_flat.values()), 1)`, so R-HP charges
`{python} cents(discount["Total"], 2)` less per kWh.

## Two load profiles

Each profile is the weighted-average annual grid kWh of a group of BGE buildings, from CAIRO's
billed kWh:

- **Profile A, existing stock:** the buildings that already heat with a heat pump in the
  ResStock baseline (upgrade 0), on their baseline load.
- **Profile B, simulated average:** every BGE building on its upgrade 1 load, ResStock's
  ENERGY STAR heat pump with electric backup applied to every building.

With flat rates, a home's shortfall is its annual kWh times the per-kWh discount, by
component.

```{python}
#| label: segments

if segment_upgrade(STATE, BATCH, SEG_R_PRECALC) != 0:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{SEG_R_PRECALC} is not upgrade 0")
if segment_upgrade(STATE, BATCH, SEG_R_CALIBRATED) != 1:
    raise RuntimeError(f"{SEG_R_CALIBRATED} is not upgrade 1")
```

```{python}
#| label: profiles


def _profile(segment: str, group: pl.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Weighted-average annual kWh for one group and its shortfall at the flat discount."""
    annual = load_billing_kwh_annual(STATE, UTILITY, BATCH, segment).collect().join(group, on="bldg_id", how="inner")
    if annual.height != group.height:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{segment}: annual kWh joined {annual.height} of {group.height} buildings")
    kwh_annual = float((annual["annual_kwh_grid"] * annual["weight"]).sum() / annual["weight"].sum())
    shortfall = {name: kwh_annual * discount[name] for name in COMPONENTS}
    shortfall["Total"] = sum(shortfall.values())
    return {"buildings": group.height, "kwh": kwh_annual, "shortfall": shortfall}


profiles = {
    "A": {
        "name": "Profile A, existing stock",
        **_profile(SEG_R_PRECALC, weights.filter(pl.col("has_hp"))),
    },
    "B": {
        "name": "Profile B, simulated average",
        **_profile(SEG_R_CALIBRATED, weights),
    },
}
for _key, _p in profiles.items():
    report_vars[f"profile_{_key}_buildings"] = _p["buildings"]
    report_vars[f"profile_{_key}_kwh"] = _p["kwh"]
    report_vars[f"profile_{_key}_shortfall"] = _p["shortfall"]

pl.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "profile": _p["name"],
            "buildings": _p["buildings"],
            "annual_kwh": _p["kwh"],
            **{f"shortfall_{name.lower()}": _p["shortfall"][name] for name in [*COMPONENTS, "Total"]},
        }
        for _p in profiles.values()
    ]
)
```

A Profile A home uses `{python} num(profiles["A"]["kwh"])` kWh a year and would pay
**`{python} dollar(profiles["A"]["shortfall"]["Total"], 2)`** less on R-HP. A Profile B home
uses `{python} num(profiles["B"]["kwh"])` kWh and would pay
**`{python} dollar(profiles["B"]["shortfall"]["Total"], 2)`** less.

### Electric resistance homes

Electric resistance homes stay on Schedule R, so they pay the added charge on every kWh. They
use more electricity than the average home, so their bill impact is larger than the mean. We
take their weighted-average annual kWh from the same CAIRO run.

```{python}
#| label: er-kwh

_er = annual_kwh_r.join(weights.filter(pl.col("heating_type") == "electrical_resistance"), on="bldg_id", how="inner")
er_homes = float(_er["weight"].sum())
er_kwh = float((_er["annual_kwh_grid"] * _er["weight"]).sum() / er_homes)
report_vars.update(er_homes=er_homes, er_kwh=er_kwh, er_buildings=_er.height)
print(f"Electric resistance homes: {_er.height} buildings, {er_homes:,.0f} customers, {er_kwh:,.0f} kWh a year")
```

An electric resistance home uses `{python} num(er_kwh)` kWh a year, against
`{python} num(kwh_total / customers)` for the average BGE home.

### Check against BGE's billed usage

BGE can't supply a representative heat pump load. Its residential heating rate codes, RH and
RLH, cover all electrically heated homes, mixing electric resistance and heat pumps, and a heat
pump uses much less electricity than resistance heat for the same heat. So the profiles above
come from ResStock. As a check on scale, we compare BGE's billed usage per heating customer,
from its response to CCAN 1-4, with ResStock's electric resistance and heat pump homes combined.

```{python}
#| label: bge-heating-kwh

_ccan = pl.read_excel(PATH_CCAN_1_4, has_header=False)
_labels = _ccan["column_1"].to_list()


def _ccan_block(header: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """The R, RH, RL and RLH rows under one block header, with the 12-month TOTAL column."""
    start = next(i for i, label in enumerate(_labels) if label and header in label.upper()) + 1
    block = _ccan.slice(start, 4).select(pl.col("column_1").alias("rate_code"), pl.col("column_14").cast(pl.Float64))
    if block.height != 4 or "TOTAL" in str(block["rate_code"].to_list()):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected CCAN 1-4 layout under {header}")
    return block


_customer_months = _ccan_block("ELECTRIC CUSTOMERS")["column_14"].to_list()
_sales = _ccan_block("KWH")["column_14"].to_list()
_heating = [1, 3]  # RH and RLH; rows 0 and 2 are R and RL
bge_heating_customers = sum(_customer_months[i] for i in _heating) / 12
bge_heating_kwh = sum(_sales[i] for i in _heating) / bge_heating_customers
bge_nonheating_kwh = sum(_sales[i] for i in (0, 2)) / (sum(_customer_months[i] for i in (0, 2)) / 12)

_electric_heat = annual_kwh_r.join(
    weights.filter(pl.col("heating_type").is_in(["electrical_resistance", "heat_pump"])), on="bldg_id"
)
resstock_electric_heat_homes = float(_electric_heat["weight"].sum())
resstock_electric_heat_kwh = float(
    (_electric_heat["annual_kwh_grid"] * _electric_heat["weight"]).sum() / resstock_electric_heat_homes
)
report_vars.update(
    bge_heating_customers=bge_heating_customers,
    bge_heating_kwh=bge_heating_kwh,
    bge_nonheating_kwh=bge_nonheating_kwh,
    resstock_electric_heat_homes=resstock_electric_heat_homes,
    resstock_electric_heat_kwh=resstock_electric_heat_kwh,
)
pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "group": ["BGE RH + RLH (heating codes)", "ResStock electric resistance + heat pump", "BGE R + RL (other codes)"],
        "customers": [bge_heating_customers, resstock_electric_heat_homes, None],
        "annual_kwh_per_customer": [bge_heating_kwh, resstock_electric_heat_kwh, bge_nonheating_kwh],
    }
)
```

BGE's heating-code customers averaged `{python} num(bge_heating_kwh)` kWh a year over the rate
year, against `{python} num(resstock_electric_heat_kwh)` for ResStock's electric resistance and
heat pump homes, `{python} pct(resstock_electric_heat_kwh / bge_heating_kwh - 1, 0)` higher. Part
of that is the class-wide gap between ResStock and BGE's sales (`{python} pct(1 / kwh_ratio - 1, 0)`,
see above). ResStock also has more electrically heated homes
(`{python} num(resstock_electric_heat_homes)`) than BGE has on heating codes
(`{python} num(bge_heating_customers)`). Not every electrically heated home is on a heating
code, so the two groups don't line up exactly. The check confirms the profiles are the right
order of magnitude; the per-kWh charge is less sensitive to the level than the dollar figures.

### Comparison with CAIRO's R-HP run

CAIRO also billed every building on R-HP in `{python} SEG_RHP_PRECALC`, on Schedule R's
month-by-month rates. For the existing heat pump homes, we compare the weighted mean difference
in the volumetric delivery bill (`elec_delivery_bill`) between the Schedule R and R-HP runs
with Profile A's flat-rate shortfall. The two differ only because flattening ignores which
months a home's kWh fall in, so they should be close.

```{python}
#| label: cross-check


def _delivery_bills(segment: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return (
        load_master_bills(STATE, BATCH, segment)
        .filter(pl.col("month") == "Annual", pl.col("sb.electric_utility") == UTILITY)
        .select("bldg_id", "elec_delivery_bill")
        .collect()
    )


_cross = (
    weights.filter(pl.col("has_hp"))
    .join(_delivery_bills(SEG_R_PRECALC), on="bldg_id")
    .join(_delivery_bills(SEG_RHP_PRECALC), on="bldg_id", suffix="_rhp")
)
cairo_shortfall = float(
    ((_cross["elec_delivery_bill"] - _cross["elec_delivery_bill_rhp"]) * _cross["weight"]).sum() / _cross["weight"].sum()
)
flat_vs_cairo = profiles["A"]["shortfall"]["Total"] / cairo_shortfall - 1
report_vars.update(cairo_shortfall_profile_A=cairo_shortfall, flat_vs_cairo=flat_vs_cairo)
print(f"Profile A shortfall, annual flat rates: ${profiles['A']['shortfall']['Total']:,.2f}")
print(f"CAIRO, monthly rates:                   ${cairo_shortfall:,.2f}")
print(f"Difference: {flat_vs_cairo:+.1%}")
if abs(flat_vs_cairo) > 0.05:
    raise RuntimeError("Flat-rate shortfall is more than 5% off CAIRO's R-HP run")
```

```{python}
#| label: monthly-rate-range

_peak_rate = max(monthly_r_total.values())
_low_rate = min(monthly_r_total.values())


def _month_span(months: list[str]) -> str:
    """'2026-01'...'2026-03' -> 'January to March 2026'; assumes consecutive months in one year."""
    first, last = (datetime.strptime(m, "%Y-%m") for m in (months[0], months[-1]))
    return f"{last:%B %Y}" if first == last else f"{first:%B} to {last:%B %Y}"


peak_months = _month_span([m for m, r in monthly_r_total.items() if r == _peak_rate])
low_months = _month_span([m for m, r in monthly_r_total.items() if r == _low_rate])
pl.DataFrame({"month": list(monthly_r_total), "schedule_r_three_charges": list(monthly_r_total.values())})
```

The flat-rate shortfall is `{python} pct(abs(flat_vs_cairo))`
`{python} "below" if flat_vs_cairo < 0 else "above"` CAIRO's month-by-month result of
`{python} dollar(cairo_shortfall, 2)`. The direction follows from the rate calendar: Schedule
R's three charges combined are highest in `{python} peak_months`
(`{python} cents(_peak_rate, 2)`) and lowest in `{python} low_months`
(`{python} cents(_low_rate, 2)`), against a flat `{python} cents(sum(schedule_r_flat.values()), 2)`.
A heat pump home uses more of its kWh in winter, so it gets more than the average discount,
and the flat rate slightly understates its shortfall. The tables below therefore lean low
for Profile A.

## How many homes enroll

We read the counts from the estimate notebook's cache. The **program floor** is the EmPOWER
heat pump systems rebated since 2017: the homes BGE could identify without attestation. It
counts systems, not homes, and some rebated systems are supplemental or cooling-only
mini-splits in homes that still heat with fossil fuel, which wouldn't qualify. So it
overstates the eligible homes behind it. It is an enrollment floor, not a lower bound on the
stock. The **stock** estimates are the whole population of homes whose main heating system is
a heat pump, which could enroll if every one attested. Between the program floor and the
central stock estimate we add four evenly spaced **illustrative steps**; they are not
estimates in their own right.

R-HP is for homes whose primary heating source is a heat pump. Hybrids with fossil backup
qualify; a fossil-heated home with one mini-split, say for cooling a garage, does not. All the
stock estimates classify homes by main heating system, so they already apply that rule.

```{python}
#| label: enrollment

_path_counts = PATH_CACHE / "bge_hp_customer_estimate_vars.pkl"
if not _path_counts.exists():
    raise RuntimeError(f"Missing {_path_counts}: render bge_hp_customer_estimate.qmd first")
counts = pickle.loads(_path_counts.read_bytes())
# The ResStock count must be on the same customer base as the weights C comes from.
_cairo_hp_homes = weights.filter(pl.col("has_hp"))["weight"].sum()
if abs(counts["stock_central"] / _cairo_hp_homes - 1) > 1e-6:
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"ResStock count {counts['stock_central']:,.0f} != CAIRO's weighted heat pump homes {_cairo_hp_homes:,.0f}"
    )

SOURCES = {
    "floor": "[BGE EmPOWER reports, 2017 to mid-2026](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket97052026_2026) (latest, p. 6; full list below)",
    "low": "[EIA RECS 2020 microdata](https://www.eia.gov/consumption/residential/data/2020/), 90% low end",
    "central": "[NREL ResStock 2024.2](https://data.openei.org/s3_viewer?bucket=oedi-data-lake&prefix=nrel-pds-building-stock%2Fend-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock%2F2024%2Fresstock_amy2018_release_2%2F)",
    "high": "[Brattle 2023](https://pub.switch.box/brattle_AssessmentElectrificationImpacts_2023), p. 50, with hybrids",
    "interpolated": "Illustrative step, not an estimate",
}
N_STEPS = 4

floor_homes = round(counts["hp_program_systems_cumulative"])
central_homes = round(counts["stock_central"])
enrollment = [
    ("Program floor", floor_homes, SOURCES["floor"]),
    *[
        (
            f"Step {step} of {N_STEPS} toward central",
            round(floor_homes + step / (N_STEPS + 1) * (central_homes - floor_homes)),
            SOURCES["interpolated"],
        )
        for step in range(1, N_STEPS + 1)
    ],
    ("Stock low (RECS 2020)", round(counts["stock_low"]), SOURCES["low"]),
    ("Stock central (ResStock)", central_homes, SOURCES["central"]),
    ("Stock high (Brattle)", round(counts["stock_high"]), SOURCES["high"]),
]
enrollment.sort(key=lambda row: row[1])
pl.DataFrame({"estimate": [r[0] for r in enrollment], "homes": [r[1] for r in enrollment]})
```

## Rate and bill impact

For each enrollment count $N$ and a profile with annual kWh $k$ and per-home shortfall $S$:

- **Revenue shortfall:** $N \times S$, by component.
- **kWh still paying:** $K - N \times k$, where $K$ is CAIRO's total residential kWh. The same
  profile's $k$ is used for the shortfall and the kWh removed, so both are on one basis.
- **Per-kWh charge:** $N \times S / (K - N \times k)$, by component, and as a share of today's
  Schedule R charge (its annual flat rate).
- **Average annual bill increase per customer still on Schedule R** (every customer that
  doesn't enroll, including heat pump homes that stay): $N \times S / (C - N)$, where $C$ is
  the customer count.
- **Annual bill increase for an electric resistance home:** the per-kWh charge times its
  annual kWh, `{python} num(er_kwh)`.

```{python}
#| label: impact


def impact(profile: dict, homes: int) -> dict:
    kwh_paying = kwh_total - homes * profile["kwh"]
    if kwh_paying <= 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{homes:,} homes remove more kWh than the class has")
    shortfall = {name: homes * profile["shortfall"][name] for name in [*COMPONENTS, "Total"]}
    charge = {name: shortfall[name] / kwh_paying for name in [*COMPONENTS, "Total"]}
    share = {name: charge[name] / schedule_r_flat[name] for name in COMPONENTS}
    share["Total"] = charge["Total"] / sum(schedule_r_flat.values())
    return {
        "homes": homes,
        "shortfall": shortfall,
        "kwh_paying": kwh_paying,
        "charge": charge,
        "share": share,
        "mean_bill": shortfall["Total"] / (customers - homes),
        "er_bill": charge["Total"] * er_kwh,
    }


_SHORTFALL_COLS = [f"shortfall_{name.lower()}" for name in [*COMPONENTS, "Total"]]
_CHARGE_COLS = [f"charge_{name.lower()}" for name in [*COMPONENTS, "Total"]]


def impact_table(profile: dict, title: str) -> GT:
    rows = []
    for label, homes, source in enrollment:
        row = impact(profile, homes)
        rows.append(
            {
                "estimate": label,
                "homes": homes,
                "source": source,
                **{col: row["shortfall"][name] for col, name in zip(_SHORTFALL_COLS, [*COMPONENTS, "Total"])},
                "kwh_paying": row["kwh_paying"],
                **{col: row["charge"][name] for col, name in zip(_CHARGE_COLS, [*COMPONENTS, "Total"])},
                "charge_share": row["share"]["Total"],
                "mean_bill": row["mean_bill"],
                "er_bill": row["er_bill"],
            }
        )
    df = pl.DataFrame(rows)
    steps = [i for i, label in enumerate(df["estimate"]) if label.startswith("Step ")]
    return (
        GT(df, rowname_col="estimate")
        .tab_header(title=title)
        .tab_stubhead(label="Enrollment estimate")
        .tab_spanner(label="Revenue BGE no longer collects, per year", columns=_SHORTFALL_COLS)
        .tab_spanner(
            label="Added charge for customers still on Schedule R, per kWh",
            columns=["kwh_paying", *_CHARGE_COLS, "charge_share"],
        )
        .tab_spanner(
            label=html("Annual bill increase for<br>customers still on Schedule R"),
            columns=["mean_bill", "er_bill"],
        )
        .cols_label(
            homes="Homes enrolled",
            source="Source",
            shortfall_distribution="Distribution",
            shortfall_transmission="Transmission",
            shortfall_empower="EmPOWER",
            shortfall_total="Total",
            kwh_paying=html("Spread over<br>(TWh)"),
            charge_distribution="Distribution",
            charge_transmission="Transmission",
            charge_empower="EmPOWER",
            charge_total="Total",
            charge_share=html("Total as % of<br>today's rate"),
            mean_bill=html("Average<br>customer"),
            er_bill=html("Electric<br>resistance home"),
        )
        .fmt_number(columns="homes", decimals=0)
        .fmt_markdown(columns="source")
        .fmt_currency(columns=_SHORTFALL_COLS, scale_by=1e-6, decimals=1, pattern="{x}M")
        .fmt_number(columns="kwh_paying", scale_by=1e-9, decimals=2)
        .fmt_number(columns=_CHARGE_COLS, scale_by=100, decimals=3, pattern="{x}¢")
        .fmt_percent(columns="charge_share", decimals=1)
        .fmt_currency(columns=["mean_bill", "er_bill"], decimals=2)
        .tab_style(style=style.text(color="#777777", style="italic"), locations=gt_loc.body(rows=steps))
        .tab_style(style=style.text(color="#777777", style="italic"), locations=gt_loc.stub(rows=steps))
        .tab_source_note(
            md(
                "Today's rate is Schedule R's distribution, transmission and EmPOWER charges "
                f"combined, as an annual flat rate ({cents(sum(schedule_r_flat.values()), 2)}). "
                "The average customer is every customer that doesn't enroll. Dollar figures are at "
                f"ResStock's usage; multiply by {kwh_ratio:.3f} for BGE's sales."
            )
        )
        .tab_options(**get_switchbox_gt_tab_options())
    )


impacts = {key: {label: impact(p, homes) for label, homes, _ in enrollment} for key, p in profiles.items()}
for _key, _rows in impacts.items():
    for _label, _row in _rows.items():
        _slug = _label.split(" (")[0].lower().replace(" ", "_")
        report_vars[f"profile_{_key}_{_slug}"] = _row
```

Each table reads left to right: how many homes enroll, the revenue BGE stops collecting from
them, the per-kWh charge that recovers it from everyone still on Schedule R, and what that
charge adds to a year's bill. The gray, italic rows are the illustrative steps between the
program floor and the central stock estimate.

### Profile A, existing stock

Each enrolled home uses `{python} num(profiles["A"]["kwh"])` kWh a year and pays
`{python} dollar(profiles["A"]["shortfall"]["Distribution"], 2)` less for distribution,
`{python} dollar(profiles["A"]["shortfall"]["Transmission"], 2)` less for transmission and
`{python} dollar(profiles["A"]["shortfall"]["EmPOWER"], 2)` less for EmPOWER, a total of
**`{python} dollar(profiles["A"]["shortfall"]["Total"], 2)`**.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-impact-profile-a

display_gt(impact_table(profiles["A"], "Profile A: existing heat pump homes move to R-HP"))
```

### Profile B, simulated average

Each enrolled home uses `{python} num(profiles["B"]["kwh"])` kWh a year and pays
`{python} dollar(profiles["B"]["shortfall"]["Distribution"], 2)` less for distribution,
`{python} dollar(profiles["B"]["shortfall"]["Transmission"], 2)` less for transmission and
`{python} dollar(profiles["B"]["shortfall"]["EmPOWER"], 2)` less for EmPOWER, a total of
**`{python} dollar(profiles["B"]["shortfall"]["Total"], 2)`**.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-impact-profile-b

display_gt(impact_table(profiles["B"], "Profile B: enrolled homes use the simulated average heat pump load"))
```

```{python}
#| label: summary-values

_a_floor = impacts["A"]["Program floor"]
_a_central = impacts["A"]["Stock central (ResStock)"]
_b_floor = impacts["B"]["Program floor"]
_b_central = impacts["B"]["Stock central (ResStock)"]
```

At the program floor of `{python} num(floor_homes)` homes, the charge for customers still on
Schedule R would rise by `{python} cents(_a_floor["charge"]["Total"])` per kWh with Profile A
(`{python} pct(_a_floor["share"]["Total"])` of today's three charges). That is
`{python} dollar(_a_floor["mean_bill"], 2)` a year for the average remaining customer and
`{python} dollar(_a_floor["er_bill"], 2)` for an electric resistance home. At the central stock
estimate of `{python} num(central_homes)` homes, it would rise by
`{python} cents(_a_central["charge"]["Total"])` per kWh
(`{python} pct(_a_central["share"]["Total"])`): `{python} dollar(_a_central["mean_bill"], 2)` a
year for the average remaining customer and `{python} dollar(_a_central["er_bill"], 2)` for an
electric resistance home. With Profile B, the same two counts give
`{python} cents(_b_floor["charge"]["Total"])` and `{python} cents(_b_central["charge"]["Total"])`
per kWh, or `{python} dollar(_b_floor["mean_bill"], 2)` and
`{python} dollar(_b_central["mean_bill"], 2)` a year for the average remaining customer.

## Data sources, assumptions and caveats

**Data sources**

- **Heat pump home counts**, as compiled in
  [`bge_hp_customer_estimate.qmd`](bge_hp_customer_estimate.qmd):
  - Program floor: residential heat pump measure quantities in BGE's EmPOWER Maryland
    semi-annual and year-end reports:
    [2017 H1](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket9154BGEs_2017) p. 24,
    [2017 H2](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket9154BGEs_2018) p. 26,
    [2018](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket94942018_2019) p. 21,
    [2019](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket94942019_2020) p. 21,
    [2020](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket94942020_2021) p. 24,
    [2021](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket96482021_2022) p. 25,
    [2022 errata](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket9648Errata_2023) p. 23,
    [2023](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket96482023_2024) pp. 22, 27,
    [2024](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket97052024_2025) p. 10,
    [2025](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket97052025_2026) p. 8,
    [2026 H1](https://pub.switch.box/bge_Docket97052026_2026) p. 6.
  - Stock low: EIA's [2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey microdata](https://www.eia.gov/consumption/residential/data/2020/),
    with its [technical documentation](https://pub.switch.box/eia_2020ResidentialEnergy_2023)
    for the method.
  - Stock central: [NREL ResStock 2024 release 2 (AMY2018)](https://data.openei.org/s3_viewer?bucket=oedi-data-lake&prefix=nrel-pds-building-stock%2Fend-use-load-profiles-for-us-building-stock%2F2024%2Fresstock_amy2018_release_2%2F),
    as modified by Switchbox (`{python} RESSTOCK_RELEASE`).
  - Stock high: [Brattle for the PSC (2023)](https://pub.switch.box/brattle_AssessmentElectrificationImpacts_2023),
    "Existing Fuel Mix by Utility", p. 50 (shares) and p. 58 (2022 customers), from the
    [AEG/Verdant 2022 survey](https://pub.switch.box/aeg_EmPOWERMarylandResidential_2023).
- **Customer count and total kWh:** CAIRO batch `{python} BATCH`, with weights scaled to
  `{python} num(customers)` customers, from Karas Exhibit E-3
  ([Karas Direct](https://pub.switch.box/karas_Docket9888Direct_2026), PDF pp. 41–42). BGE's
  test-year residential sales of `{python} f"{kwh_test_year / 1e9:,.2f}"` TWh are from the same
  exhibit, for comparison.
- **Load profiles:** CAIRO's billed annual kWh for ResStock buildings, upgrade 0 for the
  existing heat pump homes and electric resistance homes, and upgrade 1 for all homes with an
  ENERGY STAR heat pump.
- **BGE billed usage by rate code:** BGE's response to data request CCAN 1-4, Attachment 1
  (customers and kWh by month, April 2025 to March 2026), used only for the check on scale.
- **Rates:** `{python} LINK_RATES_R` (April 2025 to March 2026, flattened to the average of
  the 12 monthly rates) and the
  `{python} LINK_RATES_RHP`, both from
  rate-design-platform at commit `{python} RDP_REF`.

**Assumptions**

- R-HP is for homes whose primary heating source is a heat pump. Hybrids with fossil backup
  qualify; fossil-heated homes with a supplemental or cooling-only heat pump do not.
- Only existing heat pump homes create a shortfall. A new adopter's bill on R-HP is at least
  its old Schedule R bill plus the marginal cost of its new load, which R-HP's rates are
  calibrated to recover on average, so it keeps paying the embedded costs assigned to it.
  This holds on average, not home by home. Electric resistance homes that convert to heat
  pumps are not counted as new adopters here.
- Electric resistance homes, and heat pump homes that don't enroll, stay on Schedule R and pay.
- The shortfall is recovered on the kWh of everyone still on Schedule R, separately for
  distribution, transmission and EmPOWER, within the residential class.
- Static, one year, test-year rates. R-HP rates are applied as filed. Generation, the customer
  charge and the universal service charge are unchanged.
- Every enrolled home uses the representative profile (A or B).

**Caveats**

- The program floor counts rebated systems, not homes, and includes replacements and
  supplemental or cooling-only mini-splits in fossil-heated homes, so it overstates the
  eligible homes BGE's programs can identify. It is an enrollment floor, not a lower bound on
  the stock.
- RECS is a statewide share applied to BGE's customers, from 2020, with
  `{python} counts["recs_md_hp_respondents"]` Maryland heat pump respondents.
- The Brattle figure rests on the AEG/Verdant 2022 survey, where main heating systems are
  self-reported and some respondents may have confused heat pumps with central air
  conditioning. Its split by configuration comes from Brattle's contractor survey, not the
  survey itself. It includes hybrids, which qualify when the heat pump is the primary
  heating source.
- The enrollment counts use slightly different customer bases: RECS is applied to BGE's
  `{python} num(counts["bge_res_customers"])` March 2026 residential customers and Brattle to
  its `{python} num(counts["stock_high"] / counts["verdant_bge_hp_share_incl_hybrid"])` 2022
  customers, against the `{python} num(customers)` test-year customers used here. The gaps are
  at most `{python} pct(max(abs(counts["bge_res_customers"] / customers - 1), abs(counts["stock_high"] / counts["verdant_bge_hp_share_incl_hybrid"] / customers - 1)))`
  and are not adjusted.
- Profiles come from ResStock, not BGE: BGE's heating rate codes mix electric resistance and
  heat pump homes, so BGE can't supply a heat pump load. ResStock's electric resistance and
  heat pump homes use `{python} pct(resstock_electric_heat_kwh / bge_heating_kwh - 1, 0)` more
  kWh than BGE's heating-code customers (see the check above).
- The annual flat rate understates a winter-heavy home's discount slightly, so the Profile A
  figures lean low (`{python} pct(abs(flat_vs_cairo))` against CAIRO's monthly-rate run).
- CAIRO bills ResStock's unscaled kWh: total residential kWh is
  `{python} pct(1 / kwh_ratio - 1, 0)` above BGE's test-year sales. The per-kWh charge is
  unaffected if that gap is uniform; the dollar figures are high by the same amount (factor
  `{python} f"{kwh_ratio:.3f}"`).
- Profile A rests on `{python} num(profiles["A"]["buildings"])` ResStock buildings. Profile B is
  a simulated retrofit, mostly standard-efficiency (SEER 16 / 9.2 HSPF) equipment, and most of
  its homes keep gas water heating and appliances.
- Riders 1 and 8 true up within the residential class. Distribution revenue would be
  reallocated across classes only in a later rate case.
